step: Employer registers with INM and obtains job-offer authorization
form_name: Autorización para que extranjero desempeñe actividades lucrativas
deadline_label: At least 4–8 weeks before employee visa appointment
non_obvious_official_guidance: Employers must submit a formal job-offer request to INM and receive an authorization number (NUE) before the foreign national may apply for a Temporary Resident Worker visa at a Mexican consulate.
non_obvious_actual_reality: INM approval can take 10–30 business days. Many consulates will not schedule a visa appointment without the NUE, so delays cascade directly to the employee's start date. Newly incorporated entities in Mexico also need to pre-register as an employer with INM before the job-offer filing is accepted.
non_obvious_action_required: Register the company in INM's SIME portal, upload RFC, IMSS Registro Patronal proof, and corporate deed, then file the job-offer request. Track the NUE number and forward it to the employee for the consulate appointment.

step: Apply for Temporary Resident Worker Visa at Mexican consulate abroad
authority: Secretaría de Relaciones Exteriores (SRE) – Mexican consulate abroad
form_name: Solicitud de Visa de No Inmigrante
field_label: Visa de Residente Temporal con permiso para trabajar
deadline_label: After INM issues NUE; allow 2–4 weeks for consulate appointment
non_obvious_official_guidance: The Temporary Resident Visa with permission to work is issued by a Mexican consulate based on the employer's INM authorization (NUE). The visa is a single-entry document valid for 180 days.
non_obvious_actual_reality: The visa sticker placed in the passport is NOT the work permit and is NOT the residence card. It is only permission to enter Mexico once. The actual Tarjeta de Residente Temporal and legal authorization to work are obtained inside Mexico within 30 calendar days of arrival via the canje process at an INM office.
non_obvious_action_required: Schedule the consulate appointment immediately after receiving the NUE letter. Bring: original NUE letter, valid passport (6+ months validity), recent colour photographs (white background), proof of employment (offer letter), and any additional documents the specific consulate requests. Requirements vary by consulate post.

step: Prepare and authenticate supporting documents for visa application
field_label: Apostille / legalización y traducción oficial de documentos
deadline_label: Before consulate appointment; allow up to 8 weeks for some countries
non_obvious_official_guidance: Foreign civil documents (birth certificates, marriage certificates, criminal background check) must be apostilled under the Hague Convention or legalized through consular channels, and officially translated into Spanish by a certified perito traductor.
non_obvious_actual_reality: Criminal background checks from some countries require FBI or national police channels and can take 6–8 weeks. Apostille timelines vary significantly by origin country. Starting the process late is the single most common cause of visa delays for MX-bound workers. Some consulates require documents issued within the last 3 or 6 months.
non_obvious_action_required: Order criminal background check and apostille services as soon as the job offer is confirmed — do not wait for the INM authorization. Engage a certified Spanish translator (perito traductor oficial) in parallel. Verify the specific document age limits with your target consulate.

step: Employer confirms active IMSS Registro Patronal before employee arrival
deadline_label: Must be active before employee's first day; registration is not retroactive
non_obvious_official_guidance: Employers must hold an active IMSS Registro Patronal before they can affiliate any employee. Affiliation must be filed no later than the employee's first working day.
non_obvious_actual_reality: If the Mexican legal entity is newly incorporated for this hire, obtaining the Registro Patronal can take 2–4 weeks. IMSS affiliation cannot be applied retroactively — missing the first payroll cycle results in late-filing penalties (recargos) and actualization surcharges. Payroll systems also require the Registro Patronal to generate valid CFDI de Nómina receipts.
non_obvious_action_required: Verify the Registro Patronal is active at IMSS IDSE portal before the employee's start date. If the entity is new, initiate registration immediately on confirmation of the hire — do not wait for the INM authorization to complete.

step: Clear immigration at Mexican port of entry and confirm Residente Temporal status
form_name: Forma Migratoria Múltiple (FMM) – digital on arrival

step: Canje: exchange visa sticker for Tarjeta de Residente Temporal at INM office
field_label: Tarjeta de Residente Temporal con permiso para trabajar
deadline_label: Within 30 calendar days of entry (strict; no grace period)
non_obvious_official_guidance: Holders of a Temporary Resident Visa must present themselves at an INM office and exchange the visa sticker for a Tarjeta de Residente Temporal within 30 natural days of entry into Mexico.
non_obvious_actual_reality: INM offices in major cities (CDMX, Monterrey, Guadalajara) are heavily backlogged. Appointments on citas.inm.gob.mx must be booked within the first 24–48 hours of arrival to secure a slot before the 30-day deadline. Missing the window triggers an immigration fine and may require departure and re-entry. The physical card takes 2–4 weeks to be ready after the appointment — the receipt issued on the day is the interim work-authorization document.
non_obvious_action_required: Book the canje appointment at citas.inm.gob.mx immediately upon arrival. Required documents: original passport with visa sticker, employer letter on company letterhead, 4 colour photographs (3.5×4.5 cm, white background), INM fee payment receipt, and copies of all documents. Keep the appointment receipt as proof of pending card during the waiting period.
source: INM – Canje de visa por tarjeta de residencia

step: Obtain CURP (Clave Única de Registro de Población) certificate
deadline_label: Auto-assigned at canje; downloadable within 1–5 business days
non_obvious_official_guidance: Foreign nationals who obtain a Tarjeta de Residente Temporal are automatically assigned a CURP by RENAPO at the time of the canje filing.
non_obvious_actual_reality: The physical Tarjeta and the CURP are not available immediately. The CURP becomes searchable on the RENAPO portal (gob.mx/curp) within 1–5 business days of the canje appointment. The physical card takes 2–4 weeks. The CURP certificate downloaded from RENAPO is legally sufficient for RFC registration, IMSS affiliation, and bank account opening — do not wait for the physical card.
non_obvious_action_required: Download the CURP certificate from gob.mx/curp using passport data within 2 business days of the canje appointment. Forward it to HR for IMSS affiliation filing. If the CURP does not appear within 5 business days, visit a RENAPO module with the appointment receipt.

step: Verify permiso para trabajar notation on Tarjeta de Residente Temporal
deadline_label: At card collection (2–4 weeks after canje appointment)
non_obvious_official_guidance: The Tarjeta de Residente Temporal explicitly states whether the holder is authorized to work in Mexico ('Permiso para trabajar: Sí'). Working without this notation is a violation of immigration law regardless of visa category.
non_obvious_actual_reality: Clerical errors in the work-permit notation have occurred in practice. The card must be inspected at the INM window before leaving, as corrections require a new INM appointment and delay the employee's ability to legally start work. Employers who allow work to begin before verifying this notation share liability.
non_obvious_action_required: When collecting the Tarjeta at the INM office, verify 'Permiso para trabajar: Sí' appears on the card face before leaving the window. Photograph both sides and share with HR. If the notation is absent or incorrect, immediately file a correction request (aclaración) with INM on the same day before leaving the office.

step: Employee registers for RFC (Registro Federal de Contribuyentes) at SAT
form_name: Solicitud de inscripción al RFC – personas físicas
deadline_label: Before first payroll disbursement; within 30 days of beginning taxable activity
non_obvious_official_guidance: Foreign residents with a CURP who earn income in Mexico must register for an RFC with SAT to enable tax-compliant salary payment and ISR withholding.
non_obvious_actual_reality: SAT online self-registration requires an e.firma (digital signature) which foreign nationals typically do not yet have. In practice, the first RFC registration for a foreign worker requires an in-person appointment at a SAT Módulo de Servicios Tributarios. Without a valid RFC the CFDI de Nómina payroll receipt is rejected by SAT's validation engine, making the salary payment non-deductible for the employer and creating a payroll compliance gap.
non_obvious_action_required: Book a SAT in-person appointment immediately after receiving the CURP. Bring: CURP certificate, valid passport, Tarjeta de Residente Temporal (or receipt), and proof of address (lease or utility bill in the employee's name). The RFC (Constancia de Situación Fiscal) is issued at the appointment. Immediately provide it to HR payroll.
source: SAT – Inscripción al RFC personas físicas

step: Employer affiliates employee with IMSS and obtains Número de Seguridad Social
form_name: Aviso de Alta de trabajador (IDSE / SUA)
deadline_label: No later than first day of work

step: Employer registers employee with INFONAVIT housing fund
authority: Instituto del Fondo Nacional de la Vivienda para los Trabajadores (INFONAVIT)
form_name: Afiliación INFONAVIT (triggered automatically via IMSS IDSE filing)
deadline_label: Automatic on IMSS affiliation; first bimonthly contribution due within 2 months
non_obvious_official_guidance: Employers must contribute 5% of each employee's daily integrated salary to INFONAVIT. Registration is triggered by the same IMSS IDSE high filing and contributions are remitted bimonthly.
non_obvious_actual_reality: Although registration is automatic, employers must separately file bimonthly INFONAVIT declarations (DAIOT) and remit the 5% contribution on time. Foreign workers accrue INFONAVIT credit but access to the housing loan benefit is restricted while they hold Temporary Residency status — the contribution is still mandatory regardless.
non_obvious_action_required: Configure payroll software to calculate the 5% INFONAVIT contribution as a separate line from IMSS contributions and confirm the bimonthly payment calendar with your payroll provider. Do not assume the IMSS filing alone covers INFONAVIT reporting.

step: Open a Mexican bank account for salary receipt
authority: Comisión Nacional Bancaria y de Valores (CNBV) – via commercial bank
field_label: Cuenta de depósito en pesos mexicanos
deadline_label: As soon as CURP and RFC are available; before first payroll
non_obvious_official_guidance: Mexican banks require a valid ID (passport or residence card), CURP, RFC (Constancia de Situación Fiscal), and proof of address to open a personal current account.
non_obvious_actual_reality: Branch staff familiarity with foreign national documentation varies widely. Some branches refuse to open accounts without the physical Tarjeta de Residente Temporal; others accept the card receipt plus a downloaded CURP certificate. The RFC (Constancia de Situación Fiscal printed from SAT) is required for tax-compliant salary credits — payroll deposited without RFC linkage creates ISR compliance issues. Account opening and debit card delivery can take 1–2 weeks.
non_obvious_action_required: Bring to the branch: physical Tarjeta de Residente Temporal or card receipt, CURP certificate (downloaded from gob.mx/curp), Constancia de Situación Fiscal (RFC document from SAT), passport, and proof of Mexican address (lease or utility bill). Try two branches if the first refuses. Notify HR of the CLABE interbank code as soon as the account is open.
source: CNBV – Derechos del usuario del sistema financiero

step: Assess Mexican tax residency status (183-day rule and centre of vital interests)
field_label: Residencia fiscal en México – Art. 9 LISR
deadline_label: Before first payroll run; formally re-assess at the 183-day mark
non_obvious_official_guidance: Under Article 9 of Mexico's Ley del Impuesto Sobre la Renta (LISR), an individual is a Mexican tax resident if they spend more than 183 days in Mexico in a calendar year (contiguous or not), or if Mexico is their centre of vital interests (primary professional or family base).
non_obvious_actual_reality: Mexico applies the centre of vital interests test independently of the 183-day count. A worker whose spouse and dependants relocate to Mexico, or whose primary professional authority is exercised in Mexico, may become a tax resident from day 1 — triggering worldwide income taxation and double-taxation risk. Mexico has tax treaties with 62 countries; treaty tie-breaker rules may apply. Non-residents face flat withholding rates on Mexico-source income; residents face progressive rates on worldwide income including foreign salary paid abroad.
non_obvious_action_required: Engage a Mexican tax advisor before the first payroll run to classify the employee as resident or non-resident for withholding. If the employee has foreign-source income or overseas bank accounts, assess FATCA/CRS disclosure obligations and potential treaty relief. Document the residency determination in writing.
source: SAT – Ley del Impuesto Sobre la Renta, Art. 9

step: Employer sets up ISR payroll withholding and CFDI de Nómina issuance
form_name: CFDI de Nómina – Complemento de Nómina versión 1.2
non_obvious_official_guidance: Employers must issue a CFDI de Nómina (electronic payroll receipt) for every salary payment, stamp it through a PAC (Proveedor Autorizado de Certificación), and withhold ISR using the graduated monthly tables in Article 96 of the LISR.
non_obvious_actual_reality: The CFDI de Nómina must include the employee's RFC and CURP. Without a valid RFC the PAC rejects the document, the salary disbursement is not tax-deductible for the employer, and the employee cannot prove tax compliance. This creates strong operational pressure to complete RFC registration before the first payday — often the week after the employee starts. Payroll software must use CFDI version 3.3 with the Complemento de Nómina 1.2 schema; older formats are rejected.
non_obvious_action_required: Verify the employee's RFC is active in SAT's Lista de Contribuyentes before the first payroll run. Confirm the payroll PAC is configured for CFDI 3.3 / Complemento Nómina 1.2. Remit the monthly ISR withholding declaration to SAT by the 17th of the following month.

step: Employer remits monthly IMSS social-security contributions
form_name: SUA (Sistema Único de Autodeterminación) – cuotas obrero-patronales
field_label: Cuotas IMSS – parte patronal y obrera
deadline_label: By the 17th of the month following the contribution period

step: Employer files monthly ISR withholding provisional declaration
form_name: Declaración provisional mensual de retenciones ISR por salarios
deadline_label: By the 17th of the month following the withholding period

step: Employee files annual ISR declaration (declaración anual de personas físicas)
field_label: Ingresos por salarios; deducciones personales; crédito al salario
deadline_label: April 30 of the calendar year following the tax year
non_obvious_official_guidance: Mexican tax residents must file an annual ISR return by April 30 declaring all worldwide income for the prior calendar year. Non-residents with only single-employer Mexico-source salary may be exempt if the employer's annual adjustment covers the liability.
non_obvious_actual_reality: Employees with foreign-source income, multiple income sources, or who changed employers mid-year must file independently regardless of employer adjustments. Workers who became tax resident mid-year face a split-year calculation. Non-compliance results in recargos (surcharges), actualización (inflation adjustment), and potential audit. SAT increasingly cross-references CFDI de Nómina data with bank deposits to detect under-declared income.
non_obvious_action_required: Determine with a Mexican tax advisor each March whether an individual filing obligation exists based on the specific income mix for that year. If foreign-source income or overseas accounts exist, also assess CRS/FATCA voluntary disclosure. File by April 30 to avoid penalties.

step: Assess and mitigate Permanent Establishment (PE) risk for the foreign employer
deadline_label: Before assignment begins; reviewed annually and on any change in employee role
non_obvious_official_guidance: Under Article 2 of Mexico's LISR, a foreign company that maintains a fixed place of business in Mexico, or that habitually exercises negotiating or contracting authority through a dependent agent, may constitute a Permanent Establishment subject to Mexican corporate income tax.
non_obvious_actual_reality: A single employee with authority to sign contracts or habitually conclude transactions on behalf of the foreign parent can trigger PE regardless of whether a formal Mexican entity exists. SAT has audited intra-group service arrangements and cost-plus structures where the Mexico-based worker exercises substantive commercial decisions. Shadow payroll arrangements run through a third-party employer-of-record do not fully eliminate PE risk if the worker's actual authority is autonomous.
non_obvious_action_required: Obtain a written PE risk opinion from a qualified Mexican tax lawyer before the assignment begins. Restrict the employee's authority to conclude contracts independently. If a Mexican entity exists, document the intra-group services agreement at arm's length with a transfer pricing study. Re-evaluate PE exposure annually and when the employee's role or reporting line changes.
source: SAT – Ley del Impuesto Sobre la Renta, Art. 2

step: Renew Tarjeta de Residente Temporal before card expiry
form_name: Solicitud de Prórroga de Estancia – Residente Temporal
field_label: Renovación de Tarjeta de Residente Temporal
deadline_label: File within 30 days before card expiry; book appointment 60–90 days in advance
non_obvious_official_guidance: Temporary Resident cards are initially issued for 1 year and may be renewed annually for up to 3 additional years (4 years total). After 4 consecutive years as Temporary Resident, the individual may apply for Permanent Residency.
non_obvious_actual_reality: Renewal appointments at high-demand INM offices (especially CDMX) are difficult to secure within the 30-day window before expiry. Working after the card expires is an immigration violation even if a renewal is pending. Appointment backlogs mean practical lead time is 60–90 days. Each renewal requires an updated employer letter, pay stubs, and confirmation that the permiso para trabajar must be renewed alongside the card.
non_obvious_action_required: Diarize the card expiry date and set a reminder 90 days before expiry to book the renewal appointment at citas.inm.gob.mx. Confirm the employer can provide an updated work-authorization letter and that payroll records are current. Do not allow the card to lapse — the 4-year clock toward Permanent Residency only accrues on valid status.
source: INM – Prorroga de estancia Residente Temporal
